title: Vegan Fruit Crumble
subtitle: Oat and coconut-oil crumble topping over stewed seasonal fruit
excerpt: A fruit crumble made with coconut oil in place of butter, giving a crisp, slightly coarser topping that bakes to a golden finish over any soft, sharp seasonal fruit.
sourceNotes: A dairy-free adaptation of the classic British crumble, using solid coconut oil as the fat. The technique is identical; the result is slightly more crumbly and a fraction less rich than the butter version, but practically indistinguishable at the table once topped with plant-based cream.

recipe.batchNotes: The crumble topping can be made in large batches and kept in the fridge for up to 1 week, or frozen in portions for up to 2 months. Scatter straight from frozen onto the fruit and bake for an additional 5 minutes.

content.text: Vegan crumble uses solid coconut oil in place of butter. It behaves similarly when rubbed into the dry ingredients, it forms the same breadcrumb texture, and bakes to a crisp, golden topping with a slightly coarser bite. Any seasonal fruit works well here; frozen berries are a particularly good choice as they give more liquid during baking, which bubbles up at the edges and makes the crumble look alive at the table. Bake at 190°C for 30 to 35 minutes.

items.prepNote: solid — if your kitchen is warm, refrigerate the oil first

content.text: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Tumble the fruit into a 1.5-litre baking dish. Add the sugar and lemon juice and toss gently to combine. There is no need to pre-cook the fruit, it will cook in the oven under the crumble.

Combine the flour, oats, sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Add the coconut oil in small pieces. Using your fingertips, rub the oil into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs, some pea-sized lumps are fine and will give a pleasing crunch. If the oil is melting in a warm kitchen, refrigerate the crumble mixture for 15 minutes before using.

Scatter the crumble mixture evenly over the fruit, covering it completely. Do not press it down. Bake at 190°C for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is deep golden and the fruit juices are bubbling at the edges of the dish. Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The crumble topping is soft and not crisping
items.cause: The coconut oil was too warm and melted into the flour during mixing, preventing a crumbly texture.
items.fix: Refrigerate the crumble mixture for 15 to 20 minutes before scattering it on. Alternatively, if the crumble has already been baked soft, return to the oven without the lid for a further 5 to 10 minutes at a higher heat (210°C).

items.symptom: The fruit is watery and the crumble is sitting in liquid
items.cause: Frozen fruit released a lot of juice, or very ripe fresh fruit was used.
items.fix: Toss the fruit with 1 teaspoon of cornflour before adding to the dish, it will thicken the fruit juices as they cook.

items.symptom: The top is browning before the fruit is cooked
items.cause: The oven is running hot, or the dish is positioned too high.
items.fix: Tent with foil and continue baking until the fruit is soft and bubbling.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days, covered. Reheat in the oven at 180°C for 10 to 12 minutes until hot through and the topping has crisped again. Microwaving is possible but the crumble loses its texture.
